newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trichet not ruling out Paris hitting EMU three pct.
newsitem.headline: Trichet not ruling out Paris hitting EMU three pct.

text.p: French central bank governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Thursday the prospect of France hitting the three percent deficit goal for European monetary union should not be ruled out.
"I believe, and I think it's important, that a last little push -- and quite solid moreover, should not be excluded so that we can make three percent," Trichet told RTL radio.

He noted that Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn had made similar remarks. Strauss-Kahn has said France's latest efforts to rein in its public deficit could be helped further by a pick-up in economic growth at the end of the year.

Trichet said the Maastricht treaty should be applied on the basis of its wording but would not elaborate. The treaty sets of goal of getting public deficits to three percent of GDP but stipulates three percent, not 3.0 percent in figures.

France's audit of public finances was released earlier this week and forecast France's deficit running at a level of between 3.5 and 3.7 percent of gross domestic product this year and the government announced measures to bring it down by 0.4 percentage points.

"I noted with interest that Mr Strauss-Kahn said himself 'I think we are at the lower end of the range (of 3.5 to 3.7)'. That is, if I have understood, on the side of 3.5 percent. With the 0.4 percent (cut) that comes to around 3.1," Trichet said.

Pressed on the Maastricht treaty interpretation, he said: "The treaty should be applied according to how it is worded. I have nothing to add to that. It was worded with the possibility, a posteriori, of making a wise judgement. But a priori it seems clear to me that we have an interest in aiming for a scenario where we indeed aim for three percent or under three percent".
